description: Agent Aviation Records: submit airworthiness and directive records with the flight log and maintenance record they answer to: each airworthiness record with its id, reference, tail number, its kind (certificate or out_of_service) and the moments it starts and ends; each airworthiness directive on record against an aircraft with its id, directive number, tail number and the moments it takes effect and falls due; each directive compliance entry with its id, reference, the directive it answers, tail number, the maintenance entry behind it and the moment complied with; each maintenance entry with its id, reference, tail number and the moment signed off; each flight log entry with its id, reference, tail number and the moment flown. The signed report gives the flights and the airworthiness file, each flight against every directive standing open against its aircraft, each flight against a current airworthiness certificate on file, each compliance entry against the maintenance record behind it, and each out-of-service record against the flights the log dates inside it, and counts them, and names divergent airworthiness records: an aircraft in the flight log while an airworthiness directive in the records stands open against it, an aircraft flown with no current airworthiness record on file, a directive compliance entry with no maintenance record behind it, and an airworthiness record whose dates the flight log contradicts; then a compliance entry naming a directive the records do not hold and a directive stating no date beside flights of its aircraft, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No flight log entries, no airworthiness certificates beside flights, or no maintenance entries beside compliance entries leaves those points unverified. Tail numbers, directives and entries match by letters and digits, a directive stands open against a flight on or after the day it falls due, or the day it takes effect when it states no due day, until a compliance entry for it on that aircraft, a certificate covers a flight from the day it starts through the day it ends, and an out-of-service record contradicts a flight dated inside it. This reads whether every aircraft flew airworthy, with every directive complied with and the compliance backed by maintenance. Verdict aviation_airworthiness_divergent, aviation_airworthiness_partial, aviation_airworthiness_unverified or aviation_airworthiness_consistent. POST /api/aviation-airworthiness-check. Reads the aviation records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it flies no aircraft, inspects no aircraft in person, contacts no regulator, examiner or maintenance provider and issues no certification, which stay with the operator, its pilots, its mechanics and its regulators, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Aviation Records reads an air operator’s own records: flight log records, aircraft maintenance records, airworthiness and directive records, inspection records, pilot certificate records, training and currency records, flight duty and rest records and incident report records, each against the fleet, maintenance, pilot and duty records, the mechanic, certificate and part records, the flight log and the maintenance record, the aircraft, operations and dates flown, the schedule and the corrective entries, the required events and the currency records, the operator’s own limits, or the follow-up entries on record. The family’s ground is the paper trail behind the aircraft and the crew: what the flight log shows, what the maintenance record supports, what the certificates cover, and whether the duty and incident records hold up; it reads records about aircraft and crews, not live flight tracking and not travel booking: the Agent Travel family reads the bookings behind a trip, the Agent Agriculture Records family reads a farm’s production records and the Agent Food Safety Records family reads a food business’s safety file, while this family reads an air operator’s own records and reads none of those. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-aviation-records-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-aviation-records/.
